title: A North Pacific ventilation model calibrated without Hawaii data predicted the size of the 1988-2024 sigma0 26.5 O2 loss at Station ALOHA; the loss is inside one water type and regenerated
abstract: Question: the outcrop explanation of the North Pacific sigma0 26.5 oxygen loss was tested only at 25-46 N. Does its tracer-calibrated near-outcrop ventilation model (sci:4525c37f, calibrated with CFC-12/SF6 ages, not oxygen changes) predict an independent site? Approach: we ran the published model unchanged (8 equally good parameter sets, 3 configurations), stored its predictions at Station ALOHA (22.75 N, 158 W) and hashed them before we read any Hawaii Ocean Time-series (HOT) oxygen value. Then we computed O2, AOU, salinity and nutrients on density surfaces from 353 HOT bottle files (1988-2024) and applied six tests written in advance. Results: AOU on 26.5 rose by 21.4 umol/kg (95% interval 18.3-24.2; 2009-2024 minus 1988-1996), level until about 2000 and then about 1.1 umol/kg/yr. The model predicted 11.5-22.1 (uniform oxygen use; 9.0-34.5 over the use-rate range) and 7.7-21.6 (depth-dependent use); the best tracer-fit set gave 22.1 and 21.6. The ensemble median was about 1.5 times too small, as in the eastern regions. Salinity on 26.5 did not change (-6% of the AOU gain), the surface did not deepen, and nitrate and phosphate rose at 0.092 and 0.0076 per unit AOU, so the loss is regenerated within one water type. Non-HOT GLODAP casts near Hawaii gave +14.9 (7.0-19.2) in 2015. In the model, the lighter winter surface south of 45 N at 165 E-165 W gives 19.5 of the 22.1 umol/kg. Limitations: the size test is wide because the model sensitivity varies about 3-fold among sets; the timing and lag tests only show a shared rise, and most sets start it a few years late; the AOU peak across classes did not significantly follow outcrop loss; a lagged western-surface index did not resolve decadal phases at ALOHA (surrogate p = 0.28); one station, one surface, one late independent cruise.

Right: observed 2009-2024 minus 1988-1996 change (line and 95% interval) against each model set.
Model AOU change on sigma0 26.5 (best set, 2009-2025 minus 1988-1996), the late-winter 26.5 outcrop edge in 1965-1984 and 2005-2022, the seven earlier test regions and Station ALOHA.

ALOHA diagnostics: salinity on 26.5 did not change (water type unchanged); nitrate rises with AOU at near-Redfield ratio (regenerated); AOU change by density class against North Pacific winter outcrop area loss.

citations.reason: Model code, fields and tracer calibration used unchanged; this study tests its prediction at an independent site (Station ALOHA) and finds the observed change inside its predicted range.
Observed regional AOU series and targets on sigma0 26.5 (upstream lag test and region comparison).
Western North Pacific late-winter surface density series; its three phases were not resolved downstream at ALOHA.
Outcrop mechanism of the sigma0 26.5 oxygen loss; ALOHA adds an independent downstream site.
Eastward and downstream spread of the loss after about 1990; ALOHA starts near 1995-2000.
Loss inside water types off California; the same holds at ALOHA.
Regenerated (nutrient-backed) oxygen loss; ALOHA nitrate and phosphate rise at near-Redfield ratios.
Equivalent lighter density shift; the ALOHA AOU peak is 0.1-0.2 kg/m3 lighter than the peak of outcrop loss.
